categories.meta: New and replacement garage doors for homes in Baldwin and western Wisconsin. Raised panel, carriage house, wood-look and insulated steel doors. Free estimates: 715-928-3002.
categories.intro: New and replacement doors for attached and detached garages, from classic raised panel to carriage house and wood-look steel.
body: Your garage door is the biggest moving thing on your house, and on a lot of homes it's most of what you see from the street. We help you pick a door that fits the house and the way you use the garage, then hang it so it runs quiet and seals tight.

Most of the homes we work on want one of a few looks: raised panel for a classic front, carriage house with strap hinges and handles for a farmhouse feel, or a wood-look steel door that gives you the warmth of wood without the upkeep. Add a row of windows for light, and go insulated if you heat the garage or have a room above it.
For a replacement, we take down the old door, check the framing and seal around the opening, install new track, springs and the door, set up the opener, and haul the old door away.
points: Raised panel, long panel and carriage house styles
Wood-look steel in light oak and walnut tones
Insulated doors for heated garages and rooms above
Window rows, side stacks and decorative hardware
Old door removed and hauled away

faqs.q: Should I get an insulated garage door?
faqs.a: If the garage is attached, heated, or has a room above it, yes. An insulated door holds heat better through a Wisconsin winter, is stiffer, and runs quieter. For an unheated detached garage, a non-insulated door can be a fine way to save money. We'll lay out both at the estimate.

faqs.q: Do you haul away the old door?
faqs.a: Yes. When we replace a door, we take the old door, track and springs with us.

faqs.q: Can I see what a door will look like before I buy it?
faqs.a: Try the Door Builder on our homepage to see styles, colors and windows on different siding. Send your build with your estimate request and we'll price that door.
Yes. We'll come out, measure, talk through options and give you a written price at no charge.

categories.meta: Modern garage doors from Holldorf Garage Doors in Baldwin, WI: flush steel, full-view glass, side-stack windows and wood-look finishes in black, charcoal and more.
categories.intro: Flush panels, long glass lites and wood-look finishes. Clean-lined doors for new builds and updated homes around Baldwin.
body: Modern doors drop the raised panels for smooth, flat sections. That clean face lets color and glass do the work: black or charcoal against light siding, a stack of windows down one side, or long horizontal lites across the top.

Wood-look finishes are a big part of the modern look too. A plank-pattern steel door in walnut or light oak warms up a dark exterior and pairs well with stone and board-and-batten, without the staining and sealing real wood needs.
Modern doors show every gap and uneven line, so the install matters. We square the opening, set the track and trim tight, and adjust the door so the seams line up when it's closed.
points: Flush steel in black, charcoal, bronze and more
Full-view glass and long horizontal lites

faqs.q: Do glass garage doors let heat out?
faqs.a: Glass lets more heat through than an insulated steel section, so a full-glass door is best on garages you don't heat hard. Insulated glass and doors with fewer lites are a good middle ground. We'll walk you through the trade-off.

faqs.q: Will a dark door fade or get too hot?
faqs.a: Dark factory finishes are made for sun exposure, but dark doors do absorb more heat. On a south- or west-facing door, we'll point you to finishes and models rated for it.

faqs.q: Can a modern door go on an older house?
faqs.a: Often, yes. A flush or wood-look door can modernize an older front without a full remodel. The Door Builder on our homepage is a quick way to try it against your siding color.

categories.intro: Overhead doors for steel shops, pole buildings, barns and businesses, sized for equipment and built to open a lot.
body: A shop or pole building door works harder than a house door. It's bigger, it opens more often, and it has to clear trucks, tractors, trailers and campers. We size the door, track and spring setup for the opening and for how much the door will cycle.

We install insulated commercial-style doors with or without a window row, residential-style panel doors on hobby shops and garages, and openers that can handle the extra weight. On new post-frame and steel buildings we work with the framed opening the builder leaves us.
Already have a door that's slow, drafty, off track, or still lifted by hand? We repair and re-spring existing doors and convert manual doors to automatic.
points: Steel shops, pole buildings and barns
Tall doors for equipment, RVs and trailers
High-cycle springs for doors that open a lot

faqs.q: What size door does my shop need?
faqs.a: Measure your largest piece of equipment, then add room on each side and on top. Most hobby shops land between 10 × 10 and 12 × 12, and equipment buildings often go 14 feet or taller. We'll help you size it before the building is framed if you call early.

faqs.q: Can you install doors on a new pole building?
faqs.a: Yes. We install in the framed opening on new post-frame and steel buildings. Getting us the opening size early helps us order the right door.

faqs.q: Can you put an opener on a big shop door?
faqs.a: Yes. Larger, heavier doors need an opener rated for them, and the springs have to be balanced right first. We'll match the opener to the door.
